<!-- For pages whose Python tabs are only displayed. A page whose tabs run as
     {python} chunks includes python-tabs-run.qmd instead. -->
::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## About the Python tabs
Most code blocks on this page have an **R** and a **Python** tab, and picking one
switches the whole page. The R tab is what produced the tables and figures you see;
the Python tab is the scikit-learn equivalent, shown for translation rather than
executed by the site. Figures stay in R throughout, and a few steps with no
scikit-learn counterpart have no Python tab, which is itself worth noticing.

It is real code, not pseudocode: it runs against the same files through
`python/mlbasic_data.py`, and `python/check-snippets.py` executes every snippet in
the site to keep it honest. Expect the **numbers to differ slightly**: R and Python
draw their random splits from different generators, so the split is not the same one.
The conclusions are.
:::
